issues.title: LO-33 — ESP8266 heap measurements: getDelta() on unknown name, Storage heap suite leaves namespaces
issues.body:
Copied from https://github.com/JN0V/DomoticsCore/issues/188 for a trial of workline's line on this copy.

| LO-33 | Core, Storage | The ESP8266 heap measurements (filed 2026-09-20 by the deferred-work purge): ~~`HeapTracker::checkpoint()` samples the heap before inserting its own map node, so every window absorbs the previous checkpoint's allocation~~ (fixed 2026-10-01 with SIZE-6: the tracker gives that cost back); `getDelta()` on a name that does not exist subtracts a zero snapshot and reports a multi-kilobyte leak instead of an error; and the Storage heap suite leaves its namespaces (`heaptest`, `churn`, `overwrite`, `undrained`, `reclaim`, `nswarm`, `ns0..ns4`) resident and never shuts down the `Core` instances it builds, so successive runs start from a more fragmented heap |

Opened from `docs/CODE-ROADMAP.md`, lines 6353 to 6353 by the product-owner role.

<!-- workline:import=docs/CODE-ROADMAP.md:676c7fc0f523 -->

## Need

The maintainer needs the ESP8266 heap measurements to be trustworthy: an unknown checkpoint name must be reported as an error, and a suite run must not leave namespaces and Core instances resident, so that successive runs do not start from an ever more fragmented heap.

## Verification

- A native test calls `HeapTracker::getDelta()` with a checkpoint name that was never recorded, once as the start and once as the end. The test asserts that the caller can see an error. The native heap mock reports a non-zero free heap, so the old code subtracts a zero snapshot and returns a large number. The test fails today for that reason. The test first asserts that the recorded checkpoint has a non-zero free heap. The maintainer picks the form of the error (a sentinel value, a changed signature or a logged failure); the test pins down that form.
- A native test calls `getDelta()` with two recorded names and checks that the result is still the plain difference between them.
- Out of this work: `HeapTracker::checkpoint()`. Its own-node cost is already given back (`ownBytes_`, fixed with SIZE-6), and it is not changed here.
- The Storage heap suite `DomoticsCore-Storage/test/test_heap_esp8266/test_heap_esp8266.cpp` gets a `tearDown()` that checks that no `Core` it built is still running. Each `OpenStorage` shuts its `Core` down when it ends. A live-instance counter on `OpenStorage` goes up in the constructor and down in the destructor. `tearDown()` asserts the counter is 0, so a test that leaves a `Core` alive fails.
- After the on-device suite ends, a final test lists the Storage namespaces and asserts that these are absent: `heaptest`, `churn`, `overwrite`, `undrained`, `reclaim`, `nswarm`, `ns0` to `ns4`. Each test removes its own namespace, so the check can pass.
- Manual step on a board, which the machine cannot run: run the suite twice. Compare the free heap and the largest free block at the start of each run. Both must differ by no more than 64 bytes. A difference in the largest free block shows fragmentation that the free heap alone hides.
- When the work is done, the roadmap row LO-33 in `docs/CODE-ROADMAP.md` is marked done.

## Validation

The maintainer runs the Storage heap suite twice on a board and sees the same starting heap, and sees getDelta() on a misspelled name fail instead of showing a leak.

## Scope

The ESP8266 heap measurement tooling (HeapTracker::getDelta) and the Storage ESP8266 heap suite, which builds Cores and namespaces it never cleans up.

## Assumptions

- Assumption taken on 2026-11-04, the question of 2026-11-04 unanswered after 5 min: The reporter wants the Validation as named Given/When/Then scenarios: one for running the Storage heap suite twice and seeing the same starting heap, one for calling getDelta() on a misspelled checkpoint name and seeing an error.

No important finding open: the product owner may move it to ready.

| | | Where | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| warns | ambiguous | `#33:19` | Nit: Namespace list is partly closed and partly open — The name `ns0..ns4` and the 'ns0 to ns4' are consistent, but the test with 'nswarm' leaves the OpenStorage destructor to do the closing. 'Each test removes its own namespace' does not say how, or whether the file on LittleFS is deleted. Fix: Specify the remove call, such as deleting the file or a clear-all method. |
| warns | ambiguous | `#33:18` | Nit: 'No Core still running' check is vague — The counter in OpenStorage only counts C++ objects. It does not show that Core::begin() state was shut down. Core has no shutdown method named in the spec. One reading is that a destructor suffices; the other is that an explicit shutdown call is added. Fix: Say which Core method or destructor performs the shutdown and what the counter proves. (shows at DomoticsCore-Core/src/Core.cpp) |
| warns | out-of-scope | `#33:29` | Nit: Row names Core while Scope does not — The row title lists 'Core, Storage', and the Scope names only the tooling and the Storage suite. It is unclear whether Core changes, such as a shutdown method, are allowed. Fix: State whether Core may be changed, for example to add an explicit shutdown. |
| warns | finding-judged-no |  | dropped, from the unverifiable lens: "Manual heap comparison is not machine-checked" at #33:20 — the judge: the Verification names machine checks that would fail were the Need unmet: the `tearDown()` asserting the live `OpenStorage` counter is 0, the final test asserting `heaptest`, `churn`, ... `ns0` to `ns4` are absent, and the `getDelta()` unknown-name error test. The Need asks that no namespaces or Core instances stay resident, and the same starting heap is only the reason it gives ("so that successive runs do not start..."). (independence: model (claude-sonnet-5-5 → claude-opus-5-5)) |
